questions.title: Connect Small Ropes
questions.description:
You are given several ropes with different lengths. You can connect exactly two ropes at a time. The cost of connecting two ropes is equal to the sum of their lengths. The newly connected rope can be used again in future connections.

Your task is to return the minimum total cost required to connect all ropes into one rope.

This is a min-heap based problem because connecting the two smallest ropes first always gives the minimum total cost.

Implement the function:

Java: public int solve(int[] ropes)
Python: def solve(ropes)

Arguments:
- ropes: an array/list of positive integers where ropes[i] is the length of the i-th rope.

Return value:
- Return an integer representing the minimum total cost to connect all ropes.

Important rules:
- If there is only one rope, the cost is 0 because no connection is needed.
- Each operation must connect exactly two ropes.
- After connecting two ropes, their combined length is inserted back as a new rope.

Constraints:
- 1 <= ropes.length <= 10000
- 1 <= ropes[i] <= 10000
- The final answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

Example 1:
Input: ropes = [4,3,2,6]
Output: 29
Explanation: Connect 2 and 3 with cost 5. Ropes become [4,5,6]. Connect 4 and 5 with cost 9. Ropes become [6,9]. Connect 6 and 9 with cost 15. Total cost = 5 + 9 + 15 = 29.

Example 2:
Input: ropes = [1,2,3]
Output: 9
Explanation: Connect 1 and 2 with cost 3. Ropes become [3,3]. Connect 3 and 3 with cost 6. Total cost = 3 + 6 = 9.

questions.title: Downstream Circuit Breaker
questions.description:
A web client sends requests to two downstream services, B and C. Each service has its own circuit breaker. Your task is to simulate the circuit breaker behavior and return the result of each request.

Function signature:
Java: public List<String> solve(int[] timestamps, String[] services, String[] results)
Python: def solve(timestamps, services, results)

Arguments:
- timestamps[i] is the timestamp in seconds for the i-th request.
- services[i] is the downstream service for the i-th request. It will be either "B" or "C".
- results[i] is the actual downstream result if the request is allowed. It will be either "OK" or "FAIL".

Return value:
Return a list of strings with one entry per request: "OK", "FAIL", or "BLOCKED".

Circuit breaker rules:
- Each service has an independent circuit breaker.
- Every circuit starts in CLOSED state.
- In CLOSED state, all requests are allowed.
- When an allowed request fails in CLOSED state, record its timestamp.
- If a service has 3 or more failures within the last 600 seconds, including the current failure, its circuit moves to OPEN.
- A failure at time t is inside the sliding window if its timestamp is greater than or equal to t - 600.
- In OPEN state, requests are blocked.
- An OPEN circuit becomes HALF_OPEN when at least 300 seconds have passed since it moved to OPEN.
- In HALF_OPEN state, exactly one request is allowed.
- If the HALF_OPEN request succeeds, return "OK", move to CLOSED, and clear previous failure history for that service.
- If the HALF_OPEN request fails, return "FAIL", move back to OPEN, and reset the open timestamp to the current timestamp.

Constraints:
- 1 <= timestamps.length <= 100000
- timestamps.length == services.length == results.length
- 0 <= timestamps[i] <= 1000000000
- timestamps are non-decreasing
- services[i] is either "B" or "C"
- results[i] is either "OK" or "FAIL"

Example 1:
Input: timestamps = [0,100,200,250,499,500], services = ["B","B","B","B","B","B"], results = ["FAIL","FAIL","FAIL","OK","OK","OK"]
Output: ["FAIL","FAIL","FAIL","BLOCKED","BLOCKED","OK"]
Explanation: Service B opens at time 200 after 3 failures. Requests at 250 and 499 are blocked. At time 500, the circuit becomes HALF_OPEN and succeeds.

Example 2:
Input: timestamps = [0,10,20,30,40,41,42], services = ["B","C","B","C","B","C","C"], results = ["FAIL","FAIL","FAIL","OK","FAIL","FAIL","FAIL"]
Output: ["FAIL","FAIL","FAIL","OK","FAIL","FAIL","FAIL"]
Explanation: Services B and C are tracked independently.

questions.title: First Repeating Number
questions.description:
Given an integer array nums, return the first number that appears more than once while scanning from left to right.

If no number repeats, return -1.

Function signature:
solve(nums)

Arguments:

nums: an array/list of integers

Return value:

The first repeated integer, or -1 if there is no repeated integer.

Constraints:

1 <= nums.length <= 1000
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

Examples:

solve([2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 5]) returns 2
solve([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns -1

questions.title: First Unique Number
questions.description:
You are given an array of integers nums. Return the first number that appears exactly once in the array, based on the original left-to-right order. If every number appears more than once, return -1.

Function signature:
Java: public int solve(int[] nums)
Python: def solve(nums: list[int]) -> int

Arguments:
- nums: an array/list of integers.

Return value:
- The first integer that appears exactly once in nums.
- Return -1 if no such integer exists.

Constraints:
- 1 <= nums.length <= 1000
- -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000

Example 1:
Input: nums = [4,5,1,2,1,4,2]
Output: 5
Explanation: The counts are 4 -> 2, 5 -> 1, 1 -> 2, and 2 -> 2. The first number with count 1 is 5.

Example 2:
Input: nums = [7,7,8,8]
Output: -1
Explanation: Every number appears more than once, so there is no unique number.

questions.title: Last Stone Weight
questions.description:
You are given an array of positive integers called stones, where stones[i] represents the weight of the i-th stone. On each turn, choose the two heaviest stones and smash them together. If both stones have the same weight, both are destroyed. If they have different weights, the smaller stone is destroyed and the larger stone becomes a new stone with weight equal to the difference of the two weights. Continue until at most one stone remains. Return the weight of the final remaining stone, or 0 if no stones remain.

Function signature:
Java: public int solve(int[] stones)
Python: def solve(stones: list[int]) -> int

Arguments:
- stones: an array/list of positive integers representing stone weights.

Return value:
- An integer representing the final remaining stone weight, or 0 if all stones are destroyed.

Constraints:
- 1 <= stones.length <= 1000
- 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000

Example 1:
Input: stones = [2,7,4,1,8,1]
Output: 1
Explanation: Smash 8 and 7 to get 1. Stones become [2,4,1,1,1]. Smash 4 and 2 to get 2. Stones become [2,1,1,1]. Smash 2 and 1 to get 1. Stones become [1,1,1]. Smash 1 and 1, both disappear. One stone of weight 1 remains.

Example 2:
Input: stones = [5,5]
Output: 0
Explanation: The two stones have equal weight, so both are destroyed.

questions.title: Multi Service Rate Limiter
questions.description:
You are given a stream of API requests made to multiple services. Each request has a timestamp in seconds and a service name. A request is allowed if, during the inclusive time window [timestamp - windowSeconds + 1, timestamp], that service has fewer than maxRequests previously allowed requests. Rejected requests do not count toward future limits.

Implement the function:

Java: public boolean[] solve(int[][] requests, int maxRequests, int windowSeconds)
Python: def solve(requests, maxRequests, windowSeconds)

Arguments:
- requests: a list of requests. Each request is [timestamp, serviceId], where timestamp is a non-negative integer and serviceId is a non-negative integer representing a service.
- maxRequests: maximum allowed requests per service within the sliding window.
- windowSeconds: size of the sliding window in seconds.

Return value:
- Return a boolean array/list where true means the corresponding request is allowed and false means it is rate-limited.

Important rules:
- Requests are processed in the given order.
- Timestamps are non-decreasing.
- Each service has an independent rate limit.
- Only allowed requests count toward the limit.
- The window is inclusive. For a request at time t, allowed requests with timestamp < t - windowSeconds + 1 are outside the window and should be removed.

Constraints:
- 1 <= requests.length <= 100000
- 0 <= timestamp <= 1000000000
- 0 <= serviceId <= 100000
- 1 <= maxRequests <= 100000
- 1 <= windowSeconds <= 1000000000

Example 1:
Input: requests = [[1,10],[2,10],[3,10],[4,10]], maxRequests = 2, windowSeconds = 3
Output: [true,true,false,true]
Explanation: Service 10 allows requests at 1 and 2. At 3, the window [1,3] already has 2 allowed requests, so it is rejected. At 4, timestamp 1 is outside [2,4], so the request is allowed.

Example 2:
Input: requests = [[1,1],[1,2],[2,1],[2,2],[3,1]], maxRequests = 1, windowSeconds = 2
Output: [true,true,false,false,true]
Explanation: Services 1 and 2 are limited independently. The final request for service 1 at time 3 is allowed because time 1 is outside the window [2,3].
